summary: Pulsar 2849 is a tight, engine-building Euro where each round's drafted dice (by value and color) shape which of several parallel tracks you can advance — exploring space, developing pulsars, patenting technologies, or building transmitter networks. It rewards efficient combo-building and timing over the fixed 8 rounds more than direct competition with opponents.
praised: Clever, tense dice-drafting mechanism where value and order both matter
Deep, satisfying engine-building with multiple viable strategies
High player agency and replayability from varied tech/board setups
Elegant integration of theme (energy distribution) with mechanics
criticised: Steep learning curve and dense rulebook/iconography for a first play
Significant analysis paralysis, especially with 4 players
Player interaction is largely indirect (drafting scarcity), which can feel solitaire-ish
Turn order/dice luck can swing early-round options

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting-based scarcity

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple engines run in parallel — exploration, pulsar development, technology patents, and transmitter networks — so the winner is whoever builds the most efficient combination across these tracks.
